comments: Width sweep at 8x64 resolution (bottleneck_ch=32, vs the established default bottleneck_ch=64 point at 0.3757/0.3635 val/test dice), motivated by measured MAC headroom: 8x64 input uses only 0.83M/640M MACs at bc=64 (0.13% of budget), so even bc=384 is under 1% -- unlike native resolution, where wide96 (bc=96, 1.21x MACs) was a clean negative (0.11-0.12 dice worse) under a tight 68%-used budget. That failure doesn't necessarily transfer to 8x64: 496x fewer input pixels and near-zero budget pressure make this a genuinely different regime, untested until now. Init via kurals/expand_bottleneck_width.py (generalizes expand_kernel3.py's approach: copy every state_dict key whose shape matches the bc=64 native checkpoint, random-init the bc-dependent ones -- down2.pw, bott_c/bott_d1/bott_d2, upconv_b.dw+pw). Same recipe otherwise as kuralsnet_npu_seg_8x64_kernel3_finetune_dropout.json (norm_type=tvt, matching the established baseline exactly so this sweep isolates width alone).
